lawyer:
Amirul Islam with Idrisur Rahman and Shirin S Chowdhury, Advocates — For the Petitioner. 
Syed Abu Kawsar, Assistant Attorney-General— For the State
parties:
ARM Rafiqul Islam ----- Petitioner
Vs.
The State ----- opposite Party
full_judgment:
4. Mr. Amirul Islam, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner, submits that after being qualified in the CSS Examination in the year 1963, the petitioner joined his service as Assistant Income Tax Officer in the year 1965 after completing his in-service training and he served with dignity and reputation in all the stations in that capacity and then being promoted, also served in the capacity of Deputy Commissioner of Taxes at Dinajpur, Rangpur and Bogra. Due to his spotless and unblemished record he was further promoted as the Joint Commissioner of Taxes, Rangpur, in the year 1990 and as Additional Commissioner of Taxes in the year 1993. However the petitioner and 10 others, being permitted under the law, applied for seniority as freedom fighters and sought placement above 32 others and there being no response even after subsequent representations and on the verge of frustration being deprived of their legitimate claims, the petitioner and 20 others filed writ petition before the court but meanwhile the Administrative Tribunal being set up under new legislation, they filed case before the Administrative Tribunal but this move of the freedom fighter officers as led by the petitioner annoyed, besides others, some of the superiors of the petitioner who hatched a conspiracy against the petitioner and poisoned the car of Mr. MI Khan, Director of Inspection, who has some reservation about the freedom fighter officers and employees and then Mr. MI Khan, with a malafide intention, in April 1993 served a notice upon the petitioner asking him about the delay in submitting a report and called for the report within five days and the petitioner complied with direction given in the said notice and completed the report within time as asked. Yet Mr. MI Khan out of grudge made a complaint to the Chairman and Member of the Board of Revenue against the petitioner and misrepresented the whole facts to them and thereafter the petitioner received a show cause notice from the Member, Board of Revenue on 3-5-1993 for the delay in completing the report which the petitioner had already complied with and filed and then the Chairman of the Board of Revenue also issued another show cause notice dated 5-6-93 upon the petitioner and the said notice which was routed through Mr. MI Khan, reached the petitioner on 7-7-93 and before the said show cause notice could reach the petitioner, Mr. MI Khan on 6-7-93 appeared at the door of the petitioner early in the morning without any intimation and programme whatsoever and literally dragged the petitioner to his office by force where the petitioner was detained for his inspection till late hours without any food or facility and thereafter on 12th July, 1993 the petitioner was asked to report at Dhaka Office for preparing a report for the Tax Manual Part-1 and Part-II, and the petitioner accordingly reported on 13-7-1993 and joined the Taxes Academy, Dhaka for a short assignment of 12 days to complete his work. But just after two days i.e. 15-7-1993 the petitioner by letter dated 15-7-1993 was temporarily suspended from his service together with a discharge order from his service without any charge having been framed or for any adverse report having been made against or shown to the petitioner, and thereafter the petitioner, having realized that an enquiry committee may be constituted and Mr. MI Khan, is determined to victimize him, by letter dated 18-7-1993 prayed to the National Board of Revenue for not including Mr. MI Khan as a member of the Inquiry Committee, if any, that may be formed to make enquiry against the petitioner, but the petitioner then learned that by letter dated 17-7-1993 an enquiry committee was formed with Mr. MI Khan as its leader though petitioner did not receive any show cause notice nor any charge was framed against him. Mr. MI Khan, who worked as a Director under the Bureau of Anti-Corruption for four years, became furious to learn about the objection raised by the petitioner against his possible inclusion as a member of the Enquiry Committee and Mr. Khan then gave an open threat to the petitioner that the petitioner would be given a good lesson and thereafter Mr. MI Khan out of the personal grudge against the petitioner activated the Bureau of Anti-Corruption and influenced Mr. Nurul Islam, District Officer of Anti-Corruption Rangpur, to file a First Information Report against the petitioner and thus it will appear on the face of the record that this First Information Report was lodged against the petitioner at the instigation of Mr. MI Khan. 

 6. Mr. Islam then submits that in terms of the provision of section 151 of the aforesaid Ordinance, if the refund due to an assessee is not paid within two months of the date of the relevant assessment order or claim for refund, the government is required to pay interest at the rate 12% per annum to the assessee and accordingly being in-charge of the Ranges concerned, it was the responsibility of the petitioner to ensure that no undue delay is made in making refund so that the government is not burdened with the liability of payment of additional interest unnecessarily, so steps, if any, taken by the petitioner for timely refund of excess tax were to protect the interest of the government as part of his duty. 

 7. Regarding the allegation made in the First Information Report in respect of payment of excess amount against refund and failure to adjust Taka 34,877.00 which was in arrear, Mr. Islam submits that it was the duty of the Deputy Commissioner of Taxes of the concerned Circles to do so and in terms of the provisions of section 136 of Income Tax Ordinance 1984 the assessees who fail to adjust arrears, have to pay interest on the amount of the arrear at the rate of 15% and further in terms of the provisions of section 137 of the said Ordinance the Income Tax Department may also impose upon them penalty for a sum equal to the amount so due as arrears and accordingly in case assessees have arrear, the government is not the loser and further in terms of section 162 of the Income Tax Ordinance, if any amount is due to any person, then the amount which have been refunded or part thereof, may be set off against the taxes payable by the person under the Ordinance. 

 8. Mr. Islam then drawing our attention to the provisions of section 82 of the Income Tax Ordinance 1984 submits that no prosecution or other proceedings shall lie against any officer of the government for anything done or intended to be done under this Ordinance and that what the petitioner had done in the present case was in conformity to the provisions under this Ordinance and accordingly no prosecution can be initiated against the petitioner. Mr. Islam submits that in the present case there is no question of any loss to the government for alleged non-adjustment of the arrears and much higher amount may be realized from the assessee who has arrears. Regarding payment of excess refund to 450 assessee of five circles as alleged in the First Information Report Mr. Islam submits that there is no particulars at all in the First Information Report in this regard and in any view of the matter since none of the Deputy Commissioners of Taxes of the five Circles have been made accused’s in the present case along with the petitioner though the Deputy Commissioner Taxes of the five Circles adjudicated the claim of the concerned assessees, the prosecution has no prima facie case at all. Mr. Islam then submits that in the aforesaid facts and circumstances, even the allegations as made in the First Information Report taken as it is do not disclose any offence and further the ingredients of section 409 BPC is also not attracted in the facts and circumstances of the present case as the amount which was refunded was not entrusted with the petitioner. Mr. Islam referring to the provisions of section 405 BPC submits that by the said refund the petitioner did not misappropriate or convert the amount refunded to his own use and further there is also no breach of trust in the present case. 

 9. Mr. M Amirul Islam then referring on the decision reported in AIR 1996 (SC) page 740 submits that in the present case First Information Report was lodged on 4-8-93 but the charge sheet has not been submitted even after expiry of 180 days and the petitioner, in view of the lodging of the First Information Report, has been kept under suspension for a long time and so, in terms of the provisions of Article 35 of the Constitution, the entire proceeding is liable to be quashed and moreover, by insertion of clause 5A by Ordinance No. 111 of 1987 provisions of section 167(5) which existed before the amendment of 1992, was incorporated in the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 by way of legislation by incorporation and accordingly, in view of the principle laid down in the decision reported in AIR 1979 SC 798, the subsequent amendment made in the year 1992 to the provision of section 167(5) CrPC will not be applicable to the provisions of Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 and accordingly, in terms of section 5A of Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 the investigation being not completed within 180 days, the whole proceeding is liable to be stopped. 

 10. Mr. Syed Abu Kawsar, the learned Assistant Attorney-General appearing for the State, opposes the Rule and submits that this court cannot interfere at this stage as the case is still under investigation and section 5A of Criminal Law Amendment Act 1958 will have to be read with section 167(5) CrPC as amended in the year 1992 and so the proceeding is not liable to be stopped. 

 11. Heard the learned Advocates and perused the application filed under section 561 CrPC and the papers annexed thereto. From the provisions of section 136 of the Income Tax Ordinance 1984 it appears that in case an assessee does not pay the amount specified as payable in a notice of demand, the assessee will have to pay interest @ 15% per annum and section 137 provides that in case of default by assessee to pay arrear of taxes, a sum not exceeding that amount shall be recovered from the assessee by way of penalty. Further, in terms of the provisions of section 162, even if excess amount was refunded without adjustment, the said amount may be set off. Further from a plain reading of the provisions of sections 146 of the said Ordinance, it appears that it is Deputy Commissioner of Taxes who has to be satisfied before an order of refund as claimed by the assessee, is passed. Further, if delay is made in making the refund the government in terms of section 151 of the said Ordinance will have to pay interest to the assessee on the claimed amount at the rate of 12% per annum and so even if there is allegation against the petitioner that he has taken initiative for giving refund even then the same does not constitute an offence as thereby no loss is caused to the government and, on the other hand, it is in the interest of government that the excess amount is to be refunded to the assessees immediately so that the government is not burdened with the liability to pay any additional interest. 

 12. It thus appears that it is concerned Deputy Commissioners of Taxes of the five Circles, who after being satisfied about the claim of refund of 450 assessees, passed necessary orders and in case, refund vouchers exceeding the amount of Taka 5000.00 only, the signatures of the petitioner were obtained in those refund vouchers as required by law and further, even by this excess refund as alleged; the government was not without any remedy as the Income-Tax Department had the right to claim back the amount so refunded and thus even if it is assumed that the petitioner illegally passed the order of refund, the department can always recover the same from the assessees or this amount can be adjusted against the vouchers of taxes which the assessees are required to pay in the future assessment year. It then appears that the allegations as made in the First Information Report, even taken as it is, the same does not disclose any offence under section 409 and section 5(2) of the Anti-Corruption Act 1947 and there is also nothing to show that the petitioner was entrusted with the money which is alleged to have been paid in excess or the petitioner had domain over the said amount or that the petitioner misappropriated the said amount for his own benefit or benefit of others.
